title: Turbocharged Performance

scenes.narration: With 661 horsepower and a sub-three second dash to sixty, few cars scream performance like this one.

scenes.headline: 488 Spider
scenes.narration: Meet the 2018 Ferrari 488 Spider, an evolution from the 458, delivering more power and reduced weight.

scenes.headline: 3.9L V8 Turbo
scenes.narration: The 3.9-liter twin-turbocharged V8 churns out 561 lb-ft of torque, pushing this beast to its limits.

scenes.headline: Aerodynamics
scenes.narration: The front air intakes optimize aerodynamics, reflecting Ferrari's dedication to performance efficiency.

scenes.headline: Price Retention
scenes.narration: Originally priced around $250,000, it now fetches about $200,000, reflecting a stable annual depreciation of roughly 5%.
Ferrari's iconic quad-exhaust setup enhances the aggressive rear profile of the 488 Spider.
The air intake scoops along the rear fenders boost aerodynamics and underscore its design focus on speed.

scenes.headline: Vs. McLaren 720S
scenes.narration: Compared to the McLaren 720S Performance, which also offers 710 hp, the Ferrari maintains a unique finesse despite trailing slightly in power.
Inside, the sweeping dashboard features prominent air vents, a hallmark of Ferrari's modern design approach.

scenes.headline: Concluding Thoughts
scenes.narration: So, does the Ferrari 488 Spider's blend of Italian artistry and raw power make it worth the price tag for you?

script: With 661 horsepower and a sub-three second dash to sixty, few cars scream performance like this one. Meet the 2018 Ferrari 488 Spider, an evolution from the 458, delivering more power and reduced weight. The 3.9-liter twin-turbocharged V8 churns out 561 lb-ft of torque, pushing this beast to its limits. The front air intakes optimize aerodynamics, reflecting Ferrari's dedication to performance efficiency. Originally priced around $250,000, it now fetches about $200,000, reflecting a stable annual depreciation of roughly 5%. Ferrari's iconic quad-exhaust setup enhances the aggressive rear profile of the 488 Spider. The air intake scoops along the rear fenders boost aerodynamics and underscore its design focus on speed. Compared to the McLaren 720S Performance, which also offers 710 hp, the Ferrari maintains a unique finesse despite trailing slightly in power. Inside, the sweeping dashboard features prominent air vents, a hallmark of Ferrari's modern design approach. So, does the Ferrari 488 Spider's blend of Italian artistry and raw power make it worth the price tag for you?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2018 Ferrari 488 Spider, finished in Rosso Corsa with a beige interior. The odometer currently displays approximately 7,000 miles. This Ferrari is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report. According to the Ferrari specification plate provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes 20-inch forged wheels, carbon ceramic brakes, a sport exhaust system, a front-axle lift system, a power-retractable hardtop, Scuderia Ferrari fender shields, Daytona-style seats, carbon fiber interior trim, and a premium Hi-Fi sound system. The seller reports no notable modifications. Ferrari launched the 488 for 2016 as an evolution of the 458. Offered as a coupe and as a convertible, the model kept its predecessor's mid-mounted engine layout but received a pair of turbochargers -- displacement decreased but horsepower and torque both increased. Engineers made the 488 slightly lighter than its predecessor, while designers made several visual tweaks. Production ended in 2019. Power comes from a 3.9-liter twin-turbocharged V8, rated at 661 horsepower and 561 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
